question: What is the causative organism of leprosy?
explanation: Leprosy is specifically caused by the acid-fast bacillus Mycobacterium leprae. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why does leprosy primarily affect the skin and peripheral nerves?

options.A: These tissues have the highest concentration of blood vessels
options.B: Immune cells cannot reach the outer layers of the skin
options.C: Sweat glands provide essential nutrients for bacterial growth
options.D: The bacteria thrive in the cooler areas of the human body

explanation: Mycobacterium leprae prefers lower temperatures found in peripheral tissues and superficial skin layers. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h1)

question: How many skin lesions define the paucibacillary form of leprosy?
explanation: Paucibacillary leprosy is clinically characterized by having between one and five skin lesions. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h2)

question: A patient presents with widespread nodules and multiple anesthetic patches across the body. Which classification applies?
explanation: Widespread skin involvement, multiple lesions exceeding five, and nodular formations indicate multibacillary disease. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which staining technique is used to identify the bacteria in skin smears?
explanation: Acid-fast bacilli like Mycobacterium leprae are visualized using the Ziehl-Neelsen staining method. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which finding is considered a cardinal sign for diagnosing leprosy?

options.A: Loss of sensation in a hypopigmented skin patch
options.B: High fever with generalized joint pain
options.C: Painful ulcerations on the soles of the feet
options.D: Raised itchy wheals distributed over the trunk

explanation: Anesthetic skin lesions are one of the primary cardinal clinical signs used to confirm leprosy. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why is multidrug therapy essential in the treatment of leprosy?

options.A: To prevent the development of drug resistance
options.B: To eliminate the need for skin smear testing
options.C: To reduce the normal incubation period
options.D: To speed up the regeneration of damaged nerves

explanation: Using multiple drugs together stops the bacterium from mutating and developing resistance to single agents. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the standard treatment duration for multibacillary leprosy using MDT?
explanation: Multibacillary leprosy requires a full twelve-month course of combined medications to ensure complete bacterial eradication. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which medication is commonly prescribed to manage acute nerve inflammation in leprosy reactions?
explanation: Corticosteroids such as prednisolone are used to suppress acute inflammation and protect damaged nerves. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h5)

question: A patient with multibacillary leprosy develops painful subcutaneous nodules and fever. Which reactional state is occurring?
explanation: Erythema nodosum leprosum, or Type 2 reaction, presents with painful nodules and systemic symptoms like fever. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary reason patients with leprosy develop severe burns or cuts on their hands?

options.A: Extreme fragility of the outer skin layers
options.B: Loss of protective sensation in the extremities
options.C: Loss of blood supply to the fingertips
options.D: Complete paralysis of the upper limb muscles

explanation: Anesthesia prevents patients from feeling harmful stimuli like heat or sharp objects, leading to injuries. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which nursing intervention is most effective for preventing skin cracking in anesthetic feet?

options.A: Soaking and applying oil or cream

explanation: Regular soaking followed by moisturizing oils prevents dry skin from fissuring and developing ulcers. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h6)

question: Why do patients frequently delay seeking treatment for early leprosy symptoms?

options.A: Treatment is restricted to specialized foreign clinics
options.B: Fear of social stigma and discrimination
options.C: Initial symptoms are always intensely painful
options.D: The disease progresses too rapidly to notice

explanation: Deep-seated societal stigma often causes individuals to conceal their symptoms, leading to delayed medical intervention. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h7)

question: What key message should nurses communicate to reduce fear and encourage treatment adherence?

options.A: Medications must be taken for the rest of the patient's life
options.B: Leprosy is completely curable with multidrug therapy
options.C: Complications like nerve damage always worsen over time
options.D: Isolation is required for the entire treatment period

explanation: Emphasizing that the disease is curable helps alleviate fear and encourages patients to complete their drug regimen. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h7)
